title: Kernel-cascade reclamation for fragment-salvage and prefill-tail mitigation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Paged attention and the KV cache are a major source of tail latencies when fragile fragments trigger expensive kernel swaps or full-prefill fallbacks. We've seen 99th-percentile prefill stalls driven by small, high-fragmentation allocations that cause kernel reconfiguration and slow decode waves. Goal: implement a lightweight kernel-cascade reclamation path that (1) opportunistically salvages partially-populated KV fragments via fast in-place compaction kernels, (2) defers heavyweight kernel switches by admitting degraded but low-latency decode paths, and (3) introduces an admission and soft-quarantine policy so reclaimed fragments are validated before being used for long-lived queries. This ticket covers design, prototype, microbenchmarks, and a controlled rollout to runtime-1.19.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce observed 99th-percentile prefill tail latency for multi-tenant Paged-Attention workloads by at least 20% in synthetic workload tests
End-to-end correctness: no increase in model output divergence >0.2% on the golden prompt set after salvage reclamation enabled
CPU/GPU overhead of the reclamation path < 6% p50 increase under baseline throughput
Safe canary rollout plan documented and automated with feature flag and fallback to current kernel behavior
tasks: Design kernel-cascade state machine and fast-compaction kernel API (design doc)
Implement reclamation admission-controller and soft-quarantine metadata in KV metadata store
Add two lightweight compaction kernels (in-place micro-merge, slot-coalesce) and integrate with kernel selector
Implement decode-path fallback chain to allow degraded but low-latency decoding when kernel switch cost is high
Add metrics and tracing hooks (per-fragment lifecycle, kernel-switch latency, reclaim success rate)
Run microbenchmarks (single-tenant and multi-tenant) and compare against baseline traces
Prepare canary rollout with runtime-1.19 feature flag and playbook for rollback
comments: 2026-02-12 Maya Chen: Spike results attached. Prototype showed a 28% reduction in prefill tail on synthetic short-seq workloads using micro-merge kernel. Need to validate memory pressure impact.
2026-02-18 Arjun Patel: Implemented admission-controller scaffold and added soft-quarantine TTL metadata. Pushed initial PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9814
2026-02-24 Performance: Observed 4% GPU utilization increase at peak when reclamation runs aggressively. Tuning suggestion: add backoff based on GPU occupancy.
2026-03-03 Review (Lucia Gomez): Approved design with two caveats - ensure kernel-cascade doesn't violate KV consistency under concurrent reads; add unit tests for concurrent reclamation paths.

2026-03-08 QA: Regression test harness passed on v100 and a100 profiles. Noticed rare case where reclaimed fragment latency spikes if prefill admission fails; plan to add a fast-fail metric and immediate fallback to full-prefill
decisions: Prefer low-latency degraded decode path over immediate kernel switch when GPU kernel change cost > 12ms
Use soft-quarantine TTL of 30s for reclaimed fragments to validate reuse patterns before marking as resident
Implement reclamation as opt-in feature flag tied to runtime-1.19 for controlled rollout
notes: Next step: complete in-place compaction kernels and add unit tests for concurrent reclamation scenarios
Coordinate with observability for new trace spans: fragment.reclaim.start, fragment.reclaim.finish, kernel.switch.latency
Plan 3-stage canary: internal dev cluster -> beta customers (low qps) -> gradual ramp
